questions.s: Which angel brought the revelation of the Quran to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: Jibreel (AS) conveyed the revelation and is called Ruh al-Amin in the Quran. Mikail is associated with rain and provision, Israfil with blowing the Trumpet, and Izrail with taking souls.

questions.s: How many surahs are there in the Quran?
questions.e: The Quran has 114 surahs, from Al-Fatiha to An-Nas. 99 is the number of the well-known names of Allah, not of surahs.

questions.s: Into how many paras (juz) is the Quran divided?
questions.e: The Quran is divided into 30 equal-sized paras for convenient reading, for example one para a day in Ramadan. 60 is the number of hizb, which are half-paras.

questions.s: Which is the longest surah of the Quran?
questions.e: Al-Baqarah has 286 verses and is the longest surah. The others are long but shorter than it.

questions.s: Which of the following is the shortest surah of the Quran?
questions.e: Al-Kawthar has only three short verses. Al-Ikhlas has four, An-Nas six and Al-Fatiha seven.

questions.s: Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
questions.e: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur near Makkah. The Cave of Thawr was where he later sheltered during the Hijrah.

questions.s: The first verses revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) belong to which surah?
questions.e: The opening verses beginning with the command to read were from Surah Al-Alaq. Al-Fatiha is first in arrangement, not in revelation.

questions.s: Which surah is known as Umm al-Kitab, 'the Mother of the Book'?
questions.e: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) called Al-Fatiha Umm al-Quran, as it sums up the Quran's main themes of praise, guidance and accountability. Al-Baqarah is the longest surah, not this one.

questions.s: Who was the father of Yusuf (AS), whose story is told in Surah Yusuf?
questions.e: Yusuf (AS) was the son of Yaqub (AS), who was the son of Ishaq (AS) and grandson of Ibrahim (AS). The others are his ancestors, not his father.

questions.s: Which surah is named after the spider?
questions.e: Al-Ankabut means 'the spider'. An-Nahl is the bee, An-Naml the ant and Al-Fil the elephant.

questions.s: Which surah of the Quran does not begin with 'Bismillah'?
questions.e: Surah At-Tawbah, also called Bara'ah, is the only surah that opens without Bismillah. Al-Anfal precedes it and does begin with it.

questions.s: Surah Maryam is named after the mother of which prophet?
questions.e: Maryam (AS) was the mother of Isa (AS), who was born by the command of Allah without a father. Yahya was the son of Zakariyya (AS).

questions.s: Which of the following surahs was revealed in Madinah?
questions.e: Al-Baqarah is a Madani surah, revealed after the Hijrah, and contains many laws for the community. Al-Kahf, Maryam and Yusuf are Makki.

questions.s: Which of the following surahs was revealed in Makkah?
questions.e: Yusuf is a Makki surah. Al-Anfal, Al-Ahzab and An-Nisa are Madani, dealing with battles and community laws.

questions.s: Which theme is especially characteristic of the Makki surahs?
o: Detailed rules of inheritance among relatives
Rules for treaties with neighbouring states and rulers
Tawhid, the hereafter and the truth of prophethood
questions.e: Makki surahs mainly build faith: the oneness of Allah, the Day of Judgement and the Message. Detailed legal and social rules mostly came in Madani surahs.

questions.s: Surah Al-Ahzab refers to which battle?
questions.e: Al-Ahzab means 'the Confederates', the tribes that besieged Madinah in the Battle of the Trench.

questions.s: What event is recalled in Surah Al-Fil?
o: The flood that drowned the people of Nuh (AS) long ago
The destruction of the people of Ad
The crossing of the sea by Musa (AS)
The failed attack of Abraha's army with an elephant on the Kaaba
questions.e: Surah Al-Fil recalls how Abraha's army marched against the Kaaba and was destroyed. Flood, Ad and the sea crossing are told in other surahs.

questions.s: Whom does Surah Al-Masad condemn by name in its teaching?
questions.e: Surah Al-Masad refers to Abu Lahab, an uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) who bitterly opposed him. Abu Talib protected the Prophet (PBUH).

questions.s: What is the central theme of Surah Al-Ikhlas?
o: The detailed rules of fasting in Ramadan
questions.e: Surah Al-Ikhlas declares that Allah is One, Self-Sufficient, neither begets nor is begotten, and has no equal.

questions.s: Surah An-Nasr is connected with which great event?
o: The Hijrah of the Prophet (PBUH) to Madinah
The victory over Makkah and people entering Islam in large numbers
questions.e: An-Nasr speaks of Allah's help, victory and people entering Islam in crowds, which is associated with the conquest of Makkah.

questions.s: What is the closing message of Surah Al-Kafirun?
o: The command to fast in the month of Ramadan
The story of the People of the Cave
'To you your religion, and to me mine'
questions.e: Al-Kafirun declares that the Prophet (PBUH) will not worship what the disbelievers worship, ending with the principle that each has their own way.

questions.s: Which surah tells the story of the youths who took refuge in a cave?
questions.e: Al-Kahf means 'the Cave' and relates the story of the People of the Cave, along with other lessons.

questions.s: In Surah Al-Kahf, Musa (AS) travelled to learn from a righteous servant of Allah. By what name is this servant known in hadith?
questions.e: Hadith identify the servant as Khidr. Harun was Musa's brother and Shuayb was a prophet of Madyan.

questions.s: Under which caliph were standard copies of the Quran sent to the main provinces?
questions.e: Uthman (RA) had standard copies prepared and sent to the main cities so that all Muslims would recite from the same text.

questions.s: Which battle, in which many Quran memorisers were martyred, led Umar (RA) to urge Abu Bakr (RA) to collect the Quran in a book?
questions.e: After the many huffaz fell in the Battle of Yamama, Umar (RA) feared the loss of parts of the Quran and advised its collection. Badr, Khandaq and Tabuk were in the Prophet's lifetime.

questions.s: Who was chosen by Abu Bakr (RA) to lead the task of collecting the Quran?
questions.e: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA), a scribe of revelation who had memorised the Quran, was entrusted with the work. Abdullah ibn Masud was also a great reciter but did not lead it.

questions.s: After the caliphate of Umar (RA), who kept the original compiled copy of the Quran?
questions.e: The compiled manuscript was kept with Hafsa (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). Uthman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare standard copies. Khadijah (RA) had died long before.

questions.s: What does the word 'Quran' literally mean?
questions.e: Quran comes from an Arabic root meaning to recite, so it means 'that which is recited'.

questions.s: For about how many years was the Quran revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: Revelation continued for about 23 years: roughly 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

questions.s: In which month was the Quran first revealed?
questions.e: The Quran itself says that Ramadan is the month in which it was sent down, beginning with Laylat al-Qadr.

questions.s: According to Surah Al-Qadr, the Night of Qadr is better than
questions.e: The surah states that Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months. The other durations are not mentioned.

questions.s: What challenge does the Quran give to those who doubt its divine origin?
o: To produce a surah like it
To compose a poem in Arabic
To memorise it in one night
To translate it into their language
questions.e: The Quran challenges doubters to bring a surah like it, which no one has done. This challenge is known as tahaddi.

questions.s: In which surah does Allah promise to protect the Reminder (the Quran) from corruption?
questions.e: Surah Al-Hijr contains the promise that Allah revealed the Reminder and will Himself guard it. This is the basis of belief in the Quran's preservation.

questions.s: The Zabur was revealed to which prophet?
questions.e: The Zabur was given to Dawud (AS). His son Sulaiman (AS) was a prophet and king, but the book is attributed to Dawud.

questions.s: Which prophet built the ark by the command of Allah before the great flood?
questions.e: Nuh (AS) built the ark, and the believers and pairs of animals were carried in it when the flood came.

questions.s: Which prophet was thrown into a fire by his people but was saved when Allah made it cool and safe?
questions.e: Allah commanded the fire to be coolness and safety for Ibrahim (AS). The others faced different trials.

questions.s: Which prophet was swallowed by a large fish and called upon Allah from its belly?
questions.e: Yunus (AS) left his people without permission, was swallowed by a fish, and was saved after his supplication of repentance.

questions.s: Which prophet is known for his exemplary patience in suffering from illness and loss?
questions.e: Ayyub (AS) is remembered in the Quran as a model of patience. Allah restored his health and blessings.

questions.s: The she-camel given as a miraculous sign was associated with which prophet?
questions.e: Salih (AS) was sent to the people of Thamud, who were warned not to harm the she-camel. They killed her and were punished.

questions.s: To which people was Hud (AS) sent?
questions.e: Hud (AS) was sent to Ad. Thamud received Salih (AS), and Madyan received Shuayb (AS).

questions.s: Shuayb (AS) was sent as a prophet to which people?
questions.e: Shuayb (AS) called the people of Madyan to worship Allah and to stop cheating in weights and measures.

questions.s: Qarun, famed for his wealth that the earth swallowed, belonged to the people of which prophet?
questions.e: Qarun was from the people of Musa (AS), and his arrogance over his treasures ended in destruction.

questions.s: Whom did Iblis refuse to bow down to when Allah commanded the angels?
questions.e: Iblis refused out of pride to prostrate to Adam (AS), whom Allah had created from clay.

questions.s: How does the Quran describe the birth of Isa (AS)?
o: Like the ordinary birth of any other child in Makkah
By the command of Allah, without a father
questions.e: The Quran states that Isa (AS) was born to Maryam (AS) by Allah's command, as a sign. Surah Maryam gives the account.

questions.s: The principle 'There is no compulsion in religion' appears in which surah?
questions.e: This principle is in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:256), right after Ayat al-Kursi. Al-Kafirun speaks of separate ways but not in this phrase.

questions.s: Ayat al-Kursi, a verse about Allah's greatness, is found in which surah?
questions.e: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

questions.s: The longest verse of the Quran, found in Surah Al-Baqarah, deals with
o: the events of the Day of Judgement and its signs
questions.e: The long verse on debts instructs believers to record loans with witnesses. It is also called Ayat ad-Dayn.

questions.s: Which surah commands kindness to parents, to the extent of not saying 'uff' to them in their old age?
questions.e: Surah Al-Isra (also called Bani Israil) instructs worship of Allah alone and good conduct towards parents, including not speaking harshly to them.

questions.s: According to Surah Al-Asr, who is NOT in loss?
o: Those who gather great wealth and live in comfort
Those who believe, do good deeds and urge each other to truth and patience
Those who live the longest lives on earth
questions.e: Surah Al-Asr states that mankind is in loss except those with faith and righteous deeds who advise one another to truth and patience. Wealth, age and power are not mentioned.

questions.s: Surah Az-Zalzalah teaches that on the Day of Judgement
o: the earth will remain unchanged and calm for ever
even an atom's weight of good or evil will be seen
questions.e: The surah says whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and the same for evil. This shows complete accountability.

questions.s: In which surah is it stated that killing one innocent person is like killing all of humanity?
questions.e: Surah Al-Ma'idah (verse 32) states this principle, showing the sanctity of human life.

questions.s: Who raised the foundations of the Kaaba together with his son Ismail (AS)?
questions.e: The Quran says Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, praying that Allah accept it from them.

questions.s: In which surah did Allah command the change of the direction of prayer (qibla) towards the Kaaba?
questions.e: The command to turn towards the Sacred Mosque is in Surah Al-Baqarah, after the Muslims had prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis.

questions.s: Which surah is named after the family of Imran, the father of Maryam (AS)?
questions.e: Aal-Imran means 'the Family of Imran' and also narrates the story of Maryam (AS) and Isa (AS).

questions.s: Detailed rules of inheritance are found mainly in which surah?
questions.e: Surah An-Nisa, 'the Women', sets out shares of inheritance along with rights of orphans and women.

questions.s: Which of the following surahs begins with the letters Alif Lam Mim?
questions.e: Al-Baqarah starts with Alif Lam Mim, one of the disjointed letters (Muqatta'at). The others have no such opening.

questions.s: In which language was the Quran revealed?
questions.e: The Quran describes itself as an Arabic Quran, in clear Arabic speech.

questions.s: The Quran is also called 'Al-Furqan'. What does this mean?
o: The Criterion between right and wrong
questions.e: Furqan means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

questions.s: According to the Quran, why was it revealed gradually rather than all at once?
o: Because the Prophet (PBUH) was not able to read written text
Because Jibreel (AS) could not carry all of it at once to Makkah
To match the length of the Hijri year
To strengthen the heart of the Prophet (PBUH) and make it easier to follow
questions.e: The Quran says it was sent down in stages to strengthen the Prophet's heart, so that believers could understand and apply it step by step.

questions.s: Surah Al-Baqarah is named after
o: a camel given to Salih (AS) as a sign for Thamud
a cow in the story of Bani Israel
questions.e: Al-Baqarah means 'the Cow', after the story of the cow that Musa (AS) asked his people to sacrifice.

questions.s: The science of the rules of correct recitation of the Quran is known as
questions.e: Tajweed deals with proper pronunciation. Tafsir is commentary and fiqh is Islamic law.

questions.s: How many verses does Surah Al-Fatiha have?
questions.e: Al-Fatiha has seven verses. It is also known as Sab' al-Mathani, 'the seven oft-repeated'.

questions.s: Which surah commands believers to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah when the call for the Friday prayer is made?
questions.e: Surah Al-Jumu'ah, 'Friday', teaches this about the congregational prayer.

questions.s: Surah At-Tawbah is largely connected with which expedition?
questions.e: At-Tawbah, revealed in Madinah in the ninth year after Hijrah, speaks much about the Tabuk expedition and the hypocrites who stayed behind.

questions.s: Surah Al-Fath was revealed in connection with which event?
questions.e: Al-Fath, 'the Victory', was revealed on the return from Hudaybiyyah and described the treaty as a clear victory.

questions.s: Which surah mentions the Night Journey (Isra) in its opening verse?
questions.e: Surah Al-Isra begins by glorifying Allah who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque.

questions.s: Which prophet is called 'Khalilullah', the friend of Allah?
questions.e: The Quran says Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend (khalil).

questions.s: Which prophet is known as 'Kalimullah' because Allah spoke to him directly?
questions.e: The Quran states that Allah spoke directly to Musa (AS), giving him the title Kalimullah.

questions.s: In which surah does 'Bismillah' occur twice, once at the start and once within the text?
questions.e: In Surah An-Naml, Bismillah appears at the start and again in the letter of Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.

questions.s: Surah Al-Ma'idah takes its name from which event?
o: The crossing of the sea by Musa (AS) and his people
The request for a table spread with food
questions.e: Al-Ma'idah means 'the Table', after the disciples of Isa (AS) asked for a table of food from heaven.

questions.s: Which surah comes first in the arrangement of the Quran?
questions.e: Al-Fatiha, 'the Opening', begins the Quran. Al-Baqarah follows it, while Al-Alaq contains the first verses revealed but is placed near the end.

questions.s: Surah An-Naml takes its name from which creature?
questions.e: An-Naml means 'the ants', after the ant that warned its colony about Sulaiman (AS)'s army. Bee is An-Nahl, spider is Al-Ankabut and elephant is Al-Fil.

questions.s: Surah Al-Anfal is mainly connected with which event?
questions.e: Al-Anfal, 'the spoils of war', was revealed largely in the context of Badr and its aftermath. Uhud is discussed mainly in Aal-Imran.

questions.s: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are together called
questions.e: They are the two surahs of seeking refuge with Allah, hence Al-Mu'awwidhatayn. Az-Zahrawayn refers to Al-Baqarah and Aal-Imran.

questions.s: Why did Caliph Uthman (RA) have standard copies of the Mushaf prepared and sent to major cities?
o: Because the Quran had never been compiled before this time
To remove disputes over recitation among people in distant regions
To change the order of the surahs
To translate the Quran into Persian
questions.e: Differences in how people recited were arising across the widening Muslim lands, so Uthman (RA) unified the text in the dialect of Quraysh. The Quran had been compiled earlier and its order was not changed.

questions.s: To which prophet was the Injil revealed?
questions.e: The Injil (Gospel) was revealed to Isa (AS). The Tawrat went to Musa and the Zabur to Dawud.

questions.s: Which prophet was granted rule over the winds and the jinn and could understand the speech of birds and ants?
questions.e: The Quran describes these gifts to Sulaiman (AS). His father Dawud (AS) was also given wisdom but these particular gifts are linked to Sulaiman.

questions.s: Luqman's advice to his son, recorded in the Quran, begins with a warning against what?
o: Eating in excess at every meal
questions.e: Luqman first told his son not to join partners with Allah, calling it a great wrong. He then gave advice on prayer, patience and humility.

questions.s: Which surah forbids mocking others and backbiting?
questions.e: Surah Al-Hujurat teaches good manners, including avoiding ridicule, suspicion and backbiting.

questions.s: What is a person who has memorised the whole Quran called?
questions.e: A hafiz has committed the entire Quran to memory. A mufti gives legal opinions and a qadi judges.

questions.s: Surah Al-Baqarah has how many verses?
questions.e: Al-Baqarah consists of 286 verses. 114 is the number of surahs in the Quran.

questions.s: Which surah describes the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as the 'Seal of the Prophets' (Khatam an-Nabiyyin)?
questions.e: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:40) says Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.s: What does the term 'hadith' refer to?
o: A verse of the Quran revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) through Jibreel (AS)
A report of the sayings, actions or approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
A ruling given by a judge
questions.e: A hadith is a narration of what the Prophet (PBUH) said, did, or approved. The Quran is the revealed Word of Allah and is distinct from hadith.

questions.s: The word 'Sunnah' means
o: the way and example of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
a recitation of the Quran in the five daily prayers
questions.e: Sunnah is the practical example and way of life of the Prophet (PBUH). It is the second source of guidance after the Quran.

questions.s: Sahih Muslim was compiled by
questions.e: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj of Nishapur compiled Sahih Muslim, which is ranked with Sahih al-Bukhari as the most authentic collections.

questions.s: The two collections together known as the 'Sahihayn' are
o: Sunan Abu Dawud and Sunan an-Nasa'i
Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah
questions.e: 'Sahihayn' means 'the two Sahihs', referring to the collections of Bukhari and Muslim.

questions.s: Which of the following is one of the Six Books (Kutub al-Sittah) of hadith?
questions.e: Sunan Abu Dawud is one of the six major collections. Riyad as-Salihin is a later compilation by Imam an-Nawawi, and the other two are works of other kinds.

questions.s: Al-Muwatta, one of the earliest hadith books, was compiled in Madinah by
questions.e: Imam Malik compiled Al-Muwatta in Madinah. Imam Ahmad compiled the Musnad, and Nawawi lived centuries later.

questions.s: Who compiled the large collection known as Musnad?
questions.e: The Musnad is the work of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It contains a very large number of hadith arranged by narrator.

questions.s: Imam al-Bukhari was born in which city, from which he takes his name?
questions.e: He was born in Bukhara in Central Asia, and the name al-Bukhari means 'of Bukhara'. He later travelled widely to collect hadith.

questions.s: Which companion narrated the largest number of hadith?
questions.e: Abu Hurayrah (RA) is the best known for the greatest number of narrations. Anas and Ibn Umar also narrated many, but fewer.

questions.s: In hadith terminology, the 'isnad' is
questions.e: Isnad is the chain of narrators through whom a hadith reached the compiler. The text itself is the matn.

questions.s: The text or content of a hadith is called
questions.e: Matn is the text of the report. The chain of narrators is the isnad (or sanad), and a narrator is a rawi.

questions.s: A narrator of a hadith is called
questions.e: A rawi is one who narrates a hadith. A mufassir explains the Quran, and a qari recites it.

questions.s: What is a Hadith Qudsi?
o: A report in which the Prophet (PBUH) relates a saying of Allah in his own words
A verse of the Quran that describes the events of the hereafter
A hadith about the city of Jerusalem
questions.e: In a Hadith Qudsi the meaning is from Allah, conveyed in the Prophet's own words. Unlike the Quran, its wording is not recited in prayer.

questions.s: A collection of hadith arranged according to the companion who narrated them is called a
questions.e: In a Musnad, hadith are grouped under each Sahabi. A Sunan is organised by legal topics such as prayer and purification.

questions.s: A companion did something in the presence of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who did not object. This approval is called
questions.e: Taqrir is the silent approval of the Prophet (PBUH). Qawl is his saying and fi'l his action.

questions.s: After the Quran, what is the second source of guidance in Islam?
o: The personal writings of later historians and poets
Opinions of any scholar of any period
The Sunnah of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
questions.e: Muslims are guided first by the Quran and then by the Sunnah, which explains and applies it.

questions.s: The hadith 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself' teaches
o: strict fasting on every day of the week
questions.e: This well-known hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) makes goodwill towards others a part of true faith.

questions.s: According to a well-known hadith, who is truly strong?
o: The one who wins every contest of strength
The one who owns the most wealth
The one who speaks the loudest
The one who controls himself when angry
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that real strength lies in self-control at the time of anger, not in overpowering others.

questions.s: A hadith describes a true Muslim as one from whose tongue and hands
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said a Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other Muslims are safe, stressing good conduct.

questions.s: When asked who most deserved his good companionship, the Prophet (PBUH) first replied
questions.e: He answered 'your mother' three times before mentioning the father, showing the high status of mothers (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.s: Which of the following continues to benefit a person after death, according to a well-known hadith?
o: Wealth he left unspent in the bank
A righteous child who prays for him
questions.e: The hadith lists ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge and a righteous child who makes dua. Worldly possessions are not counted.

questions.s: The hadith 'Cleanliness is half of faith' emphasises
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said cleanliness is half of faith, a teaching that includes cleanliness of body, clothing and surroundings.

questions.s: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that Jibreel (AS) kept advising him about whom, until he thought they might be made heirs?
questions.e: The hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) shows the great importance of the rights of neighbours.

questions.s: In a well-known hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) said 'The religion is nasihah'. This means
questions.e: Nasihah means sincere advice and sincerity towards Allah, His Book, His Messenger, leaders and the common Muslims.

questions.s: According to a hadith, who are the best among the people?
o: Those who learn the Quran and teach it
Those who have gathered the most wealth in life
Those who have the most followers
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said the best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it (Bukhari).

questions.s: A hadith says that whoever does not show mercy to others
o: will gain more wealth in this world
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said the one who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.s: The Prophet (PBUH) advised his companions to
o: avoid giving good news to the people
make things easy and not difficult
questions.e: He instructed that things be made easy and that people be given glad tidings, not made to run away.

questions.s: In the Hadith of Jibreel, the Prophet (PBUH) explained 'ihsan' as
o: performing Hajj every year without fail
worshipping Allah as if you see Him
questions.e: In the Hadith of Jibreel, ihsan is to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He sees you.

questions.s: The Hadith of Jibreel, describing Islam, iman and ihsan, is narrated in Sahih Muslim by
questions.e: It is narrated from Umar (RA), who described the stranger in white clothes who asked the Prophet (PBUH) questions.

questions.s: Who compiled the well-known collection of 'Forty Hadith' (Al-Arba'in)?
questions.e: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi compiled the Forty Hadith, which cover basic principles of the faith.

questions.s: According to a hadith, for one who travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah
o: makes easy a path to Paradise
removes all hardship from the world
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Allah eases the path to Paradise for one who seeks knowledge (Sahih Muslim).

questions.s: The Prophet (PBUH) said that charity does not
questions.e: The hadith (Muslim) states that giving charity does not reduce wealth, as Allah blesses what is given.

questions.s: A 'Tabi'i' (successor) is
o: a person who lived in Makkah
a person who met a companion of the Prophet (PBUH) as a believer
a person who compiled the Quran
a person who saw the Prophet (PBUH) only once in a dream
questions.e: A Tabi'i is from the generation after the companions who met them as a believer. Meeting the Prophet (PBUH) himself makes one a Sahabi.

questions.s: A hadith reported by so many narrators in every generation that agreement on a falsehood is impossible is called
questions.e: This is the highest level of reliability. Da'if is weak, mawdu' is fabricated, and mursal has a missing companion in the chain.

questions.s: A hadith falsely attributed to the Prophet (PBUH) is called
questions.e: A fabricated report is mawdu' and must be rejected. Attributing falsehood to the Prophet (PBUH) is a serious sin.

questions.s: The Prophet (PBUH) said he was sent to
o: build large cities and grand palaces
questions.e: The well-known meaning of the hadith is that he was sent to complete good morals.

questions.s: The Prophet (PBUH) said 'The upper hand is better than the lower hand.' This means
o: the strong are the best rulers over the weak
the tall are better than the short
the one who gives is better than the one who takes
the early riser is better than the sleeper
questions.e: The upper hand is the giving hand, encouraging charity and self-reliance.

questions.s: A hadith lists those whom Allah will shade on the Day when there is no other shade. Who is among them?
o: A wealthy trader who gave nothing
A person who prayed only in public
One who judged by his own desires
questions.e: The hadith in Bukhari and Muslim begins with the just ruler and mentions a youth growing up in worship. The other options describe the opposite of such qualities.

questions.s: A hadith states that Allah does not look at your appearance and wealth but at
o: your family lines and tribal status
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that what matters before Allah is the heart and actions (Sahih Muslim).

questions.s: In which city did Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj live and work, from which he is known as an-Naysaburi?
questions.e: Imam Muslim belonged to Nishapur, in the Persian region of Khurasan, which gives him the name an-Naysaburi.

questions.s: Who compiled Sahih al-Bukhari?
questions.e: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Imam al-Bukhari. Muslim compiled Sahih Muslim, Tirmidhi the Jami', and Malik the Muwatta.

questions.s: Jami' at-Tirmidhi was compiled by
questions.e: The Jami' bears the name of its compiler, Imam Muhammad ibn Isa at-Tirmidhi. Each of the others compiled a different collection.

questions.s: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) narrated the largest number of hadith?
questions.e: Aisha (RA) narrated well over two thousand hadith and was a great scholar of the community. Khadijah (RA) passed away before the Hijrah.

questions.s: A hadith whose chain or narrators have a weakness that keeps it from the standard of authenticity is called
questions.e: Da'if means weak. Sahih is authentic, mutawatir is reported by so many that error is impossible, and Qudsi refers to a report with words from Allah.

questions.s: Which hadith is placed at the very beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari?
questions.e: Sahih al-Bukhari opens with the hadith that actions are judged by intentions, a basic principle for all deeds.

questions.s: A well-known hadith advises the believer in Allah and the Last Day to
o: speak at length on every matter
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that one who believes in Allah and the Last Day should say what is good or else remain silent.

questions.s: According to a hadith on the branches of faith, the lowest branch is
o: removing something harmful from the road
feeding the poor at every meal
questions.e: The hadith says the highest is saying La ilaha illallah and the lowest is removing something harmful from the path. Modesty is also a branch of faith.

questions.s: Which of these is a sign of a hypocrite mentioned in a well-known hadith?
o: When he is asked, he gives charity
When he fasts, he is hungry
When he travels, he prays short prayers
questions.e: The hadith says that when a hypocrite speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays. The others are ordinary acts.

questions.s: The hadith 'Islam is built upon five' is reported in Bukhari and Muslim from which companion?
questions.e: This hadith about the five pillars is narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar (RA).

questions.s: A 'Sahabi' is
o: any scholar who has narrated hadith in later times
a person who lived in Madinah in the time of the Prophet (PBUH)
a person who met the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a believer and died as a believer
questions.e: A Sahabi is one who met the Prophet (PBUH), believed in him, and died on that faith.

questions.s: According to a hadith, honesty leads to
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness to Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.s: A kind word, according to a hadith, is
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good word is sadaqah, so even those without wealth can give charity.

questions.s: In Islamic belief, 'Tawhid' means
o: the certainty of life after death
questions.e: Tawhid comes from a root meaning 'to make one'. It is belief that Allah is one, without partner or equal. The other options are separate articles of faith, not the meaning of the word.

questions.s: Which of the following is shirk, the gravest sin in Islam?
o: Treating something else as a partner of Allah
Missing a single fast because of a genuine illness
Arriving late for a family gathering after a long day
Speaking harshly to a friend in anger
questions.e: Shirk means associating partners with Allah, which contradicts Tawhid. The other choices are faults or allowed concessions, none of them shirk.

questions.s: The Kalimah Shahadah is a declaration of belief in
o: Allah's mercy and the coming Day of Judgement
the existence of the angels and of all the revealed books
the Quran as a book and the duty of Hajj
questions.e: The Shahadah states that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad (PBUH) is His messenger. Mercy, judgement, angels and books are other beliefs but are not what the Shahadah declares.

questions.s: How many obligatory prayers are Muslims required to offer every day?
questions.e: Five prayers are obligatory daily: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. Three and four are the number of rakats in some of them, not the number of prayers.

questions.s: The annual obligatory pilgrimage to Makkah is called
questions.e: Hajj is the pilgrimage made in the month of Dhul Hijjah. Zakat is the obligatory charity, sawm is fasting and tawaf is only one rite of the pilgrimage.

questions.s: The word 'zakat' conveys the sense of
questions.e: Zakat carries the meaning of purifying wealth and soul and of growth through blessing. Peace is the sense of 'Islam', struggle that of 'jihad', and thanks that of 'shukr'.

questions.s: Which angel will blow the Trumpet to announce the Day of Judgement?
questions.e: Israfil is the angel entrusted with blowing the Trumpet. Jibreel brought revelation, and Mikail is associated with rain and provision.

questions.s: Which angel is entrusted with taking the souls of people at death?
o: Israfil (AS), the angel of the Trumpet
questions.e: The Quran speaks of the Angel of Death who takes souls by Allah's command. Jibreel brought revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Mikail is associated with provision.

questions.s: According to a well-known hadith in Sahih Muslim, angels were created from
questions.e: The hadith says angels were created from light, jinn from smokeless fire, and Adam (AS) from clay. Smokeless fire is the tempting choice but describes the jinn.

questions.s: According to the Quran, the jinn were created from
questions.e: The Quran says jinn were created from smokeless fire. Clay refers to the creation of the first human being, and light refers to angels.

questions.s: Who was the first human being and the first prophet?
questions.e: Adam (AS) was created first and was also a prophet. Nuh (AS) and Ibrahim (AS) came many generations later.

questions.s: The belief in the finality of prophethood means that
o: no prophet will come after Muhammad (PBUH)
earlier prophets are to be rejected
the Quran has replaced all human reasoning
the prophets before him were not truthful
questions.e: Muslims believe Muhammad (PBUH) is the last prophet and that all earlier prophets were true messengers. Rejecting them would itself contradict Islamic belief.

questions.s: The Quran mentions the scrolls (Suhuf) given to Ibrahim (AS) and to
questions.e: The Quran mentions the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa together. The other prophets named were given no scrolls mentioned in that pairing.

questions.s: Muslims believe that the earlier revealed books, in their original form, were
o: written down by the scholars of each separate community
meant only for the rulers of those nations
from the same Allah and carried the same core message
opposed in belief to the message of the Quran
questions.e: Muslims hold that every revealed book came from Allah and called to His worship. They are not seen as opposed to the Quran, though the Quran is the final and preserved revelation.

questions.s: Belief in life after death is called belief in the
questions.e: Akhirah means the hereafter. Risalah is belief in messengers, Qadar in divine decree and Malaikah belief in angels.

questions.s: 'Risalah' as an article of faith refers to belief in
questions.e: Risalah is messengership. Belief in angels, books and the Last Day are different articles.

questions.s: The stage between a person's death and the Day of Resurrection is called
questions.e: Barzakh is the barrier or interval between death and resurrection. Mizan is the scale of deeds, and hashr is the gathering of people.

questions.s: In Islamic belief, the 'Mizan' on the Day of Judgement is
o: the bridge over which all people will have to cross
the book that records a person's life
the balance in which deeds are weighed
the plain on which people will gather
questions.e: The Mizan is the scale of justice, and no one will be wronged in it. The record of deeds is the 'kitab', and hashr is the gathering.

questions.s: 'Jannah' and 'Jahannam' refer respectively to
questions.e: Jannah means the garden of Paradise and Jahannam is Hell. The other pairs name unrelated ideas.

questions.s: The Islamic belief in Qadar teaches that
o: good deeds are never rewarded by anyone
a person need not make any effort at all
the world was made without any purpose
Allah knows all things and has decreed what will be
questions.e: Qadar is belief in Allah's knowledge and decree. It does not remove human responsibility or the need for effort.

questions.s: A student studies hard for her exam, then entrusts the result to Allah. This is an example of
questions.e: Tawakkul is making an effort and then relying on Allah for the outcome. Riya is showing off, hasad is envy and ghibah is backbiting.

questions.s: The direction Muslims face when praying is called the
questions.e: The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah. The mihrab marks it in a mosque, and the minbar is the pulpit.

questions.s: The call to prayer is known as
questions.e: The adhan is the call to prayer. The khutbah is the sermon and the takbir is the phrase 'Allahu Akbar'.

questions.s: Which congregational prayer is offered at midday on Friday in place of Zuhr?
questions.e: Jumu'ah is the weekly congregational prayer of Friday, preceded by a sermon. Tarawih belongs to Ramadan nights.

questions.s: Which obligatory prayer is offered just after sunset?
questions.e: Maghrib is offered immediately after sunset. Fajr is at dawn, Zuhr after midday and Asr in the late afternoon.

questions.s: Which obligatory daily prayer consists of three rakats?
questions.e: Maghrib has three rakats. Fajr has two, and Asr and Isha have four each.

questions.s: Ablution performed before prayer is called
questions.e: Wudu is the washing of the specified parts of the body before prayer. Iftar is the meal that ends the fast.

questions.s: In which month is the Hajj performed?
questions.e: Hajj takes place in the twelfth month, Dhul Hijjah. Ramadan is the month of fasting.

questions.s: Where do pilgrims gather on 9 Dhul Hijjah, the central day of Hajj?
questions.e: Standing at Arafat is the core of Hajj. Mina and Muzdalifah are visited on other days, and Hira is a mountain near Makkah.

questions.s: Walking seven times around the Kaaba during Hajj or Umrah is called
questions.e: Tawaf is the circling of the Kaaba. Sa'i is walking between Safa and Marwah and rami is the stoning of pillars.

questions.s: The rite of walking between Safa and Marwah recalls the search for water by
questions.e: Sa'i commemorates Hajar's running between the two hills for water for her infant son Ismail (AS). Allah then made Zamzam flow.

questions.s: The simple unstitched garments worn by male pilgrims are called
questions.e: Ihram is both the sacred state of the pilgrim and the white garments worn by men for it. The kiswah is the cloth that covers the Kaaba.

questions.s: Eid al-Adha commemorates
o: the day on which the first revelation of the Quran came
the migration of the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah
the Muslim victory over the Makkan army in the Battle of Badr in the second year after the Hijrah
the readiness of Ibrahim (AS) to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah
questions.e: Eid al-Adha recalls Ibrahim (AS)'s submission to Allah's command. The first revelation and the Hijrah are linked to other occasions, not to this Eid.

questions.s: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated at the end of
questions.e: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of the month of fasting and falls on the first of Shawwal.

questions.s: A traveller or a sick person who cannot fast during Ramadan should
o: fast twice as many days in Shawwal
fast only on the day of Eid
make up the missed days later
questions.e: The Quran allows those who are ill or travelling to complete the same number of days later. There is no penalty of doubling.

questions.s: Which of the following is NOT an obligatory act of worship in Islam?
o: Making the pilgrimage to Madinah every year
Fasting during the month of Ramadan
Giving zakat on one's qualifying wealth
questions.e: Prayer, fasting and zakat are obligatory. A visit to Madinah is encouraged but not required, and Hajj is to Makkah, once in a lifetime for those able.

questions.s: Which of the following may receive zakat according to the Quran?
questions.e: Zakat is meant for the poor, the needy and other categories named in the Quran. People who are well off do not qualify.

questions.s: Which of the following is an example of sadaqah jariyah, a continuing charity?
o: Digging a well for public use
Paying a fine for a traffic offence
Buying a gift for a friend's wedding
questions.e: A well keeps benefiting people long after it is dug, so its reward continues. The other choices are fine acts or duties but not continuing charity.

questions.s: In the Quran, riba refers to
questions.e: Riba is forbidden in the Quran. Trade is permitted. Profit from fair trade is lawful, while riba is an unjust increase on a loan.

questions.s: Which of the following is forbidden in Islam?
questions.e: The Quran calls gambling an abomination of Satan's work. Honest trade, charity and learning are encouraged.

questions.s: During a fast in Ramadan, a Muslim abstains from food and drink from
questions.e: The fasting day runs from the start of dawn until sunset. Abstaining at night is not required.

questions.s: Which is the first month of the Islamic calendar?
questions.e: The Hijri year begins with Muharram. Rabi al-Awwal is the third month.

questions.s: Each month of the Islamic calendar lasts
questions.e: Months follow the lunar cycle of about 29.5 days. The length therefore varies between 29 and 30 days.

questions.s: The Islamic lunar year is shorter than the solar year by about
questions.e: Twelve lunar months last about 354 days against about 365 days for the solar year, a difference of roughly 11 days. That is why Ramadan moves through the seasons.

questions.s: In which mosque is the Kaaba located?
questions.e: The Kaaba stands within Masjid al-Haram in Makkah. The Prophet's Mosque is in Madinah and al-Aqsa is in Jerusalem.

questions.s: A well-known hadith in Bukhari and Muslim gives special mention to three mosques. Which of these is NOT among them?
o: Masjid al-Haram in the city of Makkah
questions.e: The three are al-Haram, an-Nabawi and al-Aqsa. The Umayyad Mosque is historically important but is not named in that hadith.

questions.s: The Arabic word 'Islam' is derived from a root meaning
questions.e: Islam carries the sense of submitting to Allah and being at peace. Conquest, trade and retreat are not part of the word's meaning.

questions.s: A 'Muslim' is literally one who
questions.e: Muslim comes from the same root as Islam and means one who submits to Allah.

questions.s: Taqwa, a quality praised often in the Quran, means
o: bodily strength that is shown only in very long worship
God-consciousness and a fear of displeasing Allah
deep knowledge of the Arabic language
wealth that is spent freely on charity
questions.e: Taqwa is awareness of Allah that restrains a person from wrong and moves him to good. Strength, language skills and wealth may help but are not its meaning.

questions.s: A person bears a long illness calmly and does not complain against Allah. Which quality is shown?
questions.e: Sabr is patient endurance. Hasad is envy, ghurur is arrogance and israf is extravagance.

questions.s: 'Shukr' in Islamic ethics is
questions.e: Shukr is thankfulness shown by tongue, heart and use of one's blessings. Fear, hope and self-confidence are different attitudes.

questions.s: In Islamic terminology, an act that is permitted and carries neither reward nor punishment is called
questions.e: Mubah means permissible. Fard is obligatory, haram forbidden, and makruh disliked.

questions.s: 'Halal' means
questions.e: Halal is that which is lawful in Islam. Haram is its opposite.

questions.s: The staff that became a serpent is a miracle associated with
questions.e: The Quran tells of the staff of Musa (AS) turning into a serpent by Allah's command. Isa (AS) is associated with healing the sick, and Salih (AS) with the she-camel.

questions.s: Which of these is a miracle that the Quran attributes to Isa (AS) by Allah's permission?
o: Healing the blind and the leper
Splitting the sea for his people
Commanding the wind and the jinn
questions.e: The Quran says Isa healed the blind and the leper by Allah's leave. Splitting the sea is associated with Musa, and the cool fire with Ibrahim.

questions.s: The enduring miracle given to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is
questions.e: The Quran remains as a preserved miracle for all time. The other signs belong to earlier prophets.

questions.s: Which prophet is often called 'Abul Anbiya', the father of prophets?
questions.e: Ibrahim (AS) is known by this title because many later prophets descended from him. Adam is the first prophet, not the one given this title.

questions.s: Hajj is obligatory on a Muslim
o: once in a lifetime, if able in health and means
only after the age of sixty years
only for those who are scholars of religion
questions.e: Hajj is obligatory once for those who can afford the journey and are fit to make it. It is not required annually.

questions.s: Jibreel (AS) is called 'Ruh al-Amin' in the Quran. This means
questions.e: Ruh al-Amin means the trustworthy spirit, as Jibreel faithfully delivered Allah's message. The other titles are not his.

questions.s: The Quran calls the recording angels who write down each person's deeds
questions.e: Kiraman Katibin means noble scribes. Malik is the keeper of Hell and Ridwan of Paradise in tradition.

questions.s: Which angels are believed to question a person in the grave?
questions.e: The traditions name Munkar and Nakir as the two angels of questioning. Raqib and Atid are the recording angels.

questions.s: The Islamic greeting 'As-salamu alaykum' means
questions.e: It is a prayer for peace, and the reply is 'Wa alaykum as-salam'.

questions.s: 'Bismillah' means
questions.e: Muslims begin tasks with it. 'Alhamdulillah' means praise be to Allah.

questions.s: 'Alhamdulillah' means
o: There is no power but with Allah
questions.e: Alhamdulillah expresses gratitude and praise to Allah. 'Insha'Allah' means if Allah wills.

questions.s: The phrase 'Allahu Akbar' means
questions.e: Takbir is the declaration that Allah is greater than everything. It is used in the call to prayer and in the prayer.

questions.s: The sermon delivered before the Friday prayer is called
questions.e: The khutbah is the sermon given by the imam. A fatwa is a legal opinion.

questions.s: The person who leads the congregational prayer is called
questions.e: The imam leads the prayer. The muezzin gives the call to prayer and a hafiz is one who has memorised the Quran.

questions.s: 'Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim', two names of Allah, mean
o: the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
the Creator, the Sustainer of all
the First and the Last of all
questions.e: They come from the same root of mercy. They open every surah of the Quran except one.

questions.s: Which name of Allah means 'The Provider' or 'The Sustainer'?
questions.e: Ar-Razzaq provides sustenance to all. Al-Khaliq means the Creator and Al-Ghaffar the Oft-Forgiving.

questions.s: The name of Allah 'Al-Ghaffar' means
questions.e: Al-Ghaffar stresses that Allah forgives again and again. As-Sami is the All-Hearing.

questions.s: The 'Asma ul-Husna' are
o: the names of the great angels
the titles by which the Quran is known
the names of the major prophets
questions.e: Asma ul-Husna means the most beautiful names. The Quran asks believers to call on Allah by them.

questions.s: Islam teaches that earning a lawful livelihood honestly to support one's family is
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that honest earning, even for one's family, brings reward. Faith does not require abandoning work.

questions.s: 'Huquq al-Ibad' refers to
o: the rights owed to fellow human beings
the rights of Allah over His creation
the rules and rites of the pilgrimage
the laws of inheritance and nothing more
questions.e: It means the rights people have over one another, such as honesty and fair dealing. Islam stresses they must be fulfilled. The rights of Allah are 'Huquq Allah'.

questions.s: The Quran calls human beings 'khalifah' on earth. This idea means that humans are
o: angels who are living among men
free to spoil the earth in any way they like
stewards answerable for what Allah has entrusted
questions.e: Khalifah means vicegerent or steward. Stewardship carries responsibility, not licence to misuse.

questions.s: Islam rejects the idea of reincarnation and teaches that
o: souls return in the bodies of animals or plants
deeds will not be judged at all
every person has one worldly life, then resurrection
only the pious will be resurrected
questions.e: Islam teaches one life, death, resurrection and accountability. Rebirth in other bodies is not part of its belief.

questions.s: According to the Quran, on the Day of Judgement
o: parents will carry the sins of their children
the whole community will be judged as one
no soul will bear the burden of another
riches will outweigh the weight of deeds
questions.e: The Quran says no bearer of burdens carries another's burden. Each person answers for himself.

questions.s: The Prophet (PBUH) said that backbiting is mentioning about your brother something he would dislike. This is called
questions.e: Ghibah is speaking about an absent person in a way he would dislike, even if true. Buhtan is a false accusation, which is worse.

questions.s: Throwing pebbles at the pillars in Mina during Hajj recalls
o: the arrival of the army with the elephant at Makkah
the Muslim victory in the battle of Badr
the finding of the spring of Zamzam
questions.e: The rite recalls Ibrahim (AS) turning away Satan's attempts to dissuade him from obeying Allah. It is not linked to the other events.

questions.s: After leaving Arafat on the evening of 9 Dhul Hijjah, pilgrims proceed to
questions.e: Pilgrims spend the night at Muzdalifah, between Arafat and Mina, and then go to Mina. The other places are not part of this sequence.

questions.s: Placing the forehead on the ground in prayer is called
questions.e: Sujud is prostration. Ruku is bowing and qiyam is standing.

questions.s: Bowing with hands on the knees in prayer is called
questions.e: Ruku is the bowing posture. Sujud is prostration and qiyam is standing.

questions.s: The worldwide community of Muslims is called the
questions.e: Ummah means community or nation. Shura is consultation and qabila means tribe.

questions.s: The word 'jihad' literally means
questions.e: Jihad means striving in Allah's way, which includes the struggle against one's own faults and for justice. Hijrah is migration and qurbani is sacrifice.

questions.s: Fitrah, as used in a well-known hadith, refers to
o: the natural disposition of every newborn child
the charity given only at the end of Ramadan
a voluntary prayer offered at night
the knowledge of things that are unseen
questions.e: The hadith says every child is born on fitrah, the natural inclination towards good and belief in Allah. Sadaqat al-Fitr is a charity with a related word, which is why that option tempts.

questions.s: Which of the following describes a believer according to Islamic teaching?
o: He values wealth above everything else
He avoids everyone who disagrees with him
He is truthful, trustworthy and merciful
questions.e: Truthfulness, trust and mercy are repeatedly praised in the Quran and hadith. The other traits are condemned.

questions.s: A believer who sincerely says 'Bismillah' before eating
o: has made the food itself halal
is excused from washing the hands
must eat only a very little
questions.e: Saying it simply begins the meal with the remembrance of Allah and acknowledges His favour. It does not change the ruling of food.

questions.s: 'Yawm ad-Din', a name for the Last Day, means
o: the Day of Gathering for trade
questions.e: Din here means recompense or reckoning. On that day everyone receives the result of their deeds.

questions.s: The well of Zamzam is located
o: on the plain of Mount Arafat
inside the Cave of Hira near Makkah
close to the Kaaba, inside Masjid al-Haram
questions.e: Zamzam is within the precincts of Masjid al-Haram. It is linked with Hajar and Ismail (AS).

questions.s: The Quran states that Allah created the heavens and the earth in
questions.e: Several verses say that creation took place in six 'ayyam', meaning periods. The seven here recalls the seven heavens, which is why it tempts.

questions.s: Outwardly professing faith while inwardly denying it is called
questions.e: Nifaq is hypocrisy. Ikhlas is sincerity, and zuhd is detachment from worldly excess.

questions.s: In which month do Muslims observe the obligatory fast?
questions.e: The obligatory fast is kept in Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. Shawwal follows Ramadan and begins with Eid al-Fitr.

questions.s: Which book was revealed to Musa (AS)?
questions.e: The Tawrah was revealed to Musa (AS). The Zabur was given to Dawud (AS) and the Injil to Isa (AS).

questions.s: According to the Quran, those given their record of deeds in the right hand on the Day of Judgement
o: will be sent back to the world
will have to wait for forgiveness
questions.e: The Quran describes those given the record in the right hand as joyful and successful. Being given it in the left hand is a sign of loss.

questions.s: What may a Muslim do if water is not available for wudu?
o: Skip the prayer until water is found
Wash with any liquid that is available
Offer the prayer without any purification
questions.e: The Quran allows tayammum, a symbolic purification with clean earth, when water cannot be had. Prayer is not simply dropped.

questions.s: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, falls in which month?
questions.e: Laylat al-Qadr is in Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was first revealed. Shaban is the month before Ramadan.

questions.s: Which month of the Islamic calendar follows Ramadan?
questions.e: Shawwal is the tenth month. Shaban precedes Ramadan, and Dhul Qadah comes after Shawwal.

questions.s: Sincere tawbah (repentance) requires a person to
o: only recite words of apology aloud
wait until old age before repenting
feel regret, stop the sin and resolve not to return to it
give up all worldly work and every kind of trade
questions.e: Scholars of every school describe repentance as regret, abandoning the sin and a firm resolve not to return. Words alone, without change, are not enough.

questions.s: The Kaaba is also called
questions.e: Bayt Allah means the House of Allah. Bayt al-Maqdis is Jerusalem, and Dar al-Arqam was an early meeting house.

questions.s: 'Insha'Allah' is said when speaking about
o: an event that has already happened
a greeting of peace to a friend
a future plan, meaning if Allah wills
questions.e: It acknowledges that the future is in Allah's hands. The Quran teaches saying it when promising to do something.

questions.s: 'Amanah' in Islamic ethics refers to
o: a debt that may be ignored if unpaid
a trust that is to be honoured and returned
a gift that must always be kept completely secret
a punishment given for a major crime
questions.e: Amanah is something entrusted to a person, such as property, a secret or an office, which must be kept faithfully. Betraying it is a grave moral failing.

questions.s: The day of Eid al-Adha is the
questions.e: Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul Hijjah, after the day of Arafat. The 1st of Ramadan is the first day of fasting.

questions.s: The core message that every prophet brought, according to the Quran, was to
o: follow the same laws of worship in detail
questions.e: Prophets differed in their laws but agreed on Tawhid. Every messenger called people to worship Allah alone.

questions.s: In which city was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah, in the Arabian Peninsula, and received his mission there.

questions.s: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: His father was Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib, who passed away before the Prophet (PBUH) was born. Abdul Muttalib was his grandfather.

questions.s: What was the name of the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb. Khadijah (RA) was his first wife, and Halimah was his foster mother.

questions.s: Who took care of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the death of his mother?
o: His uncle Abu Lahab, a leader of the Quraysh
questions.e: After his mother Aminah died, he was raised by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, and then by his uncle Abu Talib.

questions.s: Who became the guardian of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after Abdul Muttalib died?
questions.e: Abu Talib, the father of Ali (RA), took charge of the Prophet (PBUH) and protected him later in Makkah as well.

questions.s: To which tribe did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) belong?
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Banu Hashim clan of Quraysh. Aws and Khazraj were the tribes of Madinah.

questions.s: Who was the foster mother who nursed the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert?
o: Aminah bint Wahb, his own mother
questions.e: Infants of Makkah were often sent to nurse among desert tribes, and Halimah of Banu Sa'd cared for him. Umm Ayman was his attendant later.

questions.s: By which title was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) known among the Quraysh before prophethood?
o: Dhun-Nurayn, the Possessor of Two Lights
questions.e: Even his opponents called him Al-Amin and As-Sadiq for his honesty. Al-Faruq was later the title of Umar (RA) and Siddiq of Abu Bakr (RA).

questions.s: What was the occupation of Khadijah (RA) when the Prophet (PBUH) married her?
o: A teacher of children in the city of Makkah
questions.e: Khadijah (RA) was a respected businesswoman of Makkah who hired the honest Muhammad (PBUH) to take her goods to Syria.

questions.s: How did the Prophet (PBUH) settle the Quraysh dispute over who would place the Black Stone when the Kaaba was rebuilt?
o: He placed it on a cloth and let leaders of the clans lift it together, then set it in place himself
He asked the oldest man of Makkah to place it alone
He let the clans draw lots
He placed it alone without discussion
questions.e: The Quraysh accepted his wise solution, which avoided bloodshed. Every clan shared in the honour.

questions.s: At about what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
questions.e: He received the first revelation at the age of forty in the Cave of Hira. At 63 he passed away.

questions.s: Who was the first person to believe in the message of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: Khadijah (RA) believed at once and comforted him after the first revelation. Others soon followed.

questions.s: Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) is known as 'As-Siddiq'?
questions.e: Abu Bakr (RA) was called As-Siddiq, the one who always confirmed the truth, especially after the Mi'raj.

questions.s: Which house in Makkah was used by the early Muslims as a meeting place for teaching?
questions.e: The house of Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam near Safa was used for meetings. Dar an-Nadwa was the Quraysh council hall.

questions.s: Who is regarded as the first martyr in Islam, killed in Makkah for her faith?
questions.e: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar and wife of Yasir, was killed by the Quraysh because she would not give up her faith.

questions.s: Which companion, tortured by the Quraysh for refusing to give up Islam, later became the first caller to prayer (muadhdhin)?
questions.e: Bilal (RA) endured being laid on hot sand and was freed by Abu Bakr (RA). He gave the first adhan in Madinah.

questions.s: To which land did a group of Muslims first migrate to escape persecution in Makkah?
questions.e: In the fifth year of prophethood a group migrated to Abyssinia, where a just king gave them protection.

questions.s: By what title is the just Christian king of Abyssinia who gave refuge to the Muslims known?
questions.e: The ruler of Abyssinia was the Negus, who sheltered the Muslims. Heraclius was the Byzantine emperor and Khosrau the Persian.

questions.s: Which companion, whose conversion strengthened the Muslims, was given the title 'Al-Faruq'?
questions.e: Umar (RA) accepted Islam in Makkah, and his boldness gave courage to the Muslims. He was called Al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood.

questions.s: For about how long did the Quraysh keep up their social boycott of the Banu Hashim in the valley of Abu Talib?
questions.e: The boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib lasted about three years, until it was ended and the document was set aside.

questions.s: The 'Year of Sorrow' refers to the year in which the Prophet (PBUH) lost
questions.e: Within a short time both his supportive wife Khadijah (RA) and his protecting uncle Abu Talib died, making it a time of great grief.

questions.s: Why did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travel to Ta'if in the tenth year of prophethood?
o: To perform Hajj with the people of Ta'if
To trade with the merchants of Ta'if
To seek support for Islam, though the people treated him harshly
To fight the tribe of Thaqif
questions.e: He went to invite the people of Ta'if to Islam after losing protection in Makkah, but they rejected him and drove him out with stones.

questions.s: What did Allah prescribe for the Muslims at the time of the Mi'raj?
questions.e: The five daily prayers were enjoined during the Mi'raj, the Prophet's ascent through the heavens. Fasting, zakat and Hajj were prescribed later.

questions.s: The two Pledges of Aqabah were made with people from which city?
questions.e: Believers from Yathrib met the Prophet (PBUH) at Aqabah near Mina and pledged to protect him, which prepared the Hijrah.

questions.s: Which companion was sent to Madinah as a teacher before the Hijrah to teach Islam to its people?
questions.e: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) taught Quran and invited the people of Madinah to Islam, and many of the Aws and Khazraj accepted.

questions.s: In which year CE did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madinah?
questions.e: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE and marks the first year of the Islamic calendar. 630 CE is the conquest of Makkah and 632 CE his death.

questions.s: Before the Hijrah, the city of Madinah was known as
questions.e: Madinah was called Yathrib, and it became 'Madinat an-Nabi' (the city of the Prophet) after the Hijrah.

questions.s: In which cave did the Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take shelter on their way to Madinah?
questions.e: They stayed three days in the Cave of Thawr to evade the Quraysh before moving towards Madinah.

questions.s: Which was the first mosque built by the Prophet (PBUH) after migrating?
questions.e: He built the Mosque of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah on arriving. Masjid an-Nabawi was built after he settled in the city.

questions.s: Who started the Hijri calendar, with the year of the Hijrah as its first year?
questions.e: The Hijri calendar was adopted in the caliphate of Umar (RA), who chose the Hijrah as the starting point.

questions.s: The Muslims of Madinah who welcomed and helped those who migrated are called
questions.e: The helpers of Madinah are the Ansar. Those who migrated from Makkah are the Muhajirun.

questions.s: The pairing of each migrant (Muhajir) with a helper (Ansari) as brothers is known as
questions.e: Mu'akhat means brotherhood, which helped settle the migrants and strengthened unity.

questions.s: The Charter of Madinah was an agreement that
o: ended the war between Madinah and Makkah for ever
set out the rights and duties of the Muslims, Jews and other tribes living in Madinah
questions.e: The charter made the groups of Madinah a single community with a common defence and mutual obligations.

questions.s: In which year after the Hijrah was the Battle of Badr fought?
questions.e: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE). Uhud was in 3 AH and the Trench in 5 AH.

questions.s: Approximately how many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
questions.e: About 313 Muslims faced a force of around 1,000 from Makkah. The figures 700 and 3,000 belong to the armies at Uhud.

questions.s: What led to the early setback for the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud?
o: The Muslims ran out of water at the battlefield
A group of archers left their post on the hill
questions.e: The archers left the pass after the Quraysh seemed to be retreating, and Khalid ibn al-Walid, then fighting for the Quraysh, attacked from behind.

questions.s: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
questions.e: Hamza (RA), known as the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud. Abbas lived long after, and Abu Talib had died in Makkah.

questions.s: Who suggested digging a trench around Madinah in the Battle of the Trench?
questions.e: Salman al-Farsi (RA) suggested the trench, a defence method known in Persia, and the Muslims dug it before the confederates arrived.

questions.s: The pledge taken by the companions beneath a tree before the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah is called
questions.e: Bay'at ar-Ridwan, the Pledge of Satisfaction, was mentioned by Allah in the Quran with approval.

questions.s: In which year after the Hijrah was the Battle of Khaybar fought?
questions.e: Khaybar was fought in 7 AH, after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, against the fortresses north of Madinah.

questions.s: Who was appointed first commander of the Muslim army at the Battle of Mu'tah?
questions.e: Zayd ibn Haritha (RA) was the first commander, followed by Ja'far and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. Khalid took over after they were martyred.

questions.s: The conquest of Makkah took place in which year after the Hijrah?
questions.e: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan, 8 AH (630 CE), after the Quraysh broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

questions.s: How did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) treat the people of Makkah on its conquest?
questions.e: He forgave those who had persecuted him for years, and most of Makkah then entered Islam.

questions.s: The expedition of Tabuk in 9 AH was undertaken because of
o: the threat of a Byzantine army on the northern border
a rebellion by the tribes in the far south of Yemen
questions.e: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards the northern frontier after the news of the Byzantine army. It is also called the Expedition of Hardship.

questions.s: In which year after the Hijrah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform the Farewell Pilgrimage?
questions.e: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH. He passed away a few months after it, in 11 AH.

questions.s: Which principle was stated in the Holy Prophet's (PBUH) Farewell Sermon?
o: No Arab has superiority over a non-Arab except by piety
The wealthy have greater rights than the poor in every matter
questions.e: In the sermon at Arafat he declared the equality of all people, with superiority only in taqwa, and abolished interest and tribal vengeance.

questions.s: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
questions.e: He passed away at the age of 63, after 23 years of prophethood.

questions.s: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) buried?
o: In the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur
In the room of Aisha (RA) beside the Mosque in Madinah
questions.e: He passed away in the house of Aisha (RA) and was buried in the same room. It is today inside Masjid an-Nabawi.

questions.s: For about how many years did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) call people to Islam in Makkah after the first revelation?
questions.e: He preached in Makkah for about thirteen years and in Madinah for about ten, making twenty-three years.

questions.s: Which daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was married to Ali (RA)?
questions.e: Fatimah (RA), the youngest daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Khadijah (RA), married Ali (RA). Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum were each married to Uthman (RA).

questions.s: The son of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Ibrahim, was born to which wife?
questions.e: Ibrahim was born in Madinah to Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (RA) and died in infancy. The other children of the Prophet (PBUH) were from Khadijah (RA).

questions.s: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA)?
questions.e: Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA). Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Umar (RA).

questions.s: Which widow did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry soon after the death of Khadijah (RA)?
questions.e: Sawdah (RA) was the first wife after Khadijah (RA), then Aisha (RA). Zaynab bint Jahsh married the Prophet (PBUH) in Madinah.

questions.s: The mosque in Madinah where the direction of prayer was changed from Jerusalem towards the Kaaba is known as
questions.e: Masjid al-Qiblatayn, 'the Mosque of the Two Qiblas', commemorates the change of direction during prayer.

questions.s: Which companion received the title 'Sayf Allah' (the Sword of Allah) from the Prophet (PBUH) at Mu'tah?
questions.e: After the first three commanders were martyred, Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) led the army, and the Prophet (PBUH) called him Sayf Allah.

questions.s: Which Qurayshi leader was killed in the Battle of Badr?
questions.e: Abu Jahl was among the Quraysh leaders killed at Badr. Abu Lahab died in Makkah soon afterwards, and Abu Sufyan later embraced Islam.

questions.s: In seerah terminology, a 'ghazwah' is a military expedition
o: led only by Abu Bakr (RA) in the days of his caliphate
in which the Prophet (PBUH) himself took part
questions.e: Ghazwah refers to campaigns in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part, as in Badr or Uhud. Those he sent others to lead are called sariyyah.

questions.s: The period of ignorance in Arabia before Islam is called
questions.e: Jahiliyyah is the period before Islam, when idolatry and injustice were common.

questions.s: At about the age of twelve, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled with Abu Talib on a trade journey to
questions.e: He accompanied his uncle Abu Talib on a caravan to Syria, where the monk Bahira is reported to have noticed signs of his future prophethood.

questions.s: At which place between Makkah and Madinah did the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
questions.e: Aminah died at Abwa on the way back from visiting Madinah, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about six years old.

questions.s: The year in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born is known as
o: the Year of Sorrow after the death of Khadijah (RA)
questions.e: He was born in the year Abraha's elephant army marched against the Kaaba, so it is called the Year of the Elephant.

questions.s: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: He married Khadijah (RA) before the first revelation, and she remained his only wife until her death.

questions.s: From which hill did the Prophet (PBUH) first publicly call the Quraysh to Islam?
questions.e: After about three years of private invitation, he called the Quraysh from Mount Safa near the Kaaba.

questions.s: Who spoke for the Muslims before the king of Abyssinia?
questions.e: Ja'far (RA) explained Islam before the king and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved the Negus.

questions.s: In the Night Journey (Isra), the Prophet (PBUH) was taken from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to
o: The Quba Mosque on the outskirts of Madinah
questions.e: The Isra was the journey from Masjid al-Haram to Al-Aqsa, followed by the ascent (Mi'raj) through the heavens.

questions.s: Who slept in the bed of the Prophet (PBUH) on the night of the Hijrah to mislead the Quraysh?
questions.e: Ali (RA) lay in the Prophet's bed so the Quraysh would think he was still there. Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH).

questions.s: Which companion hosted the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in his house on arrival in Madinah?
questions.e: The Prophet's she-camel stopped near the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA), who hosted him until Masjid an-Nabawi and his rooms were built.

questions.s: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah established
o: the end of the Hijrah and return to Makkah
a ten-year truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh
questions.e: The treaty in 6 AH set a truce, and the Muslims were to return the next year to perform Umrah. It later opened the way to peaceful spread of Islam.

questions.s: The Battle of Hunayn was fought soon after the conquest of Makkah against
questions.e: Hunayn was fought in 8 AH against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif. The Byzantines were involved at Mu'tah and Tabuk.

questions.s: In which year after the Hijrah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
questions.e: He passed away in Rabi al-Awwal, 11 AH (632 CE). The Farewell Pilgrimage had been in 10 AH.

questions.s: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet (PBUH) sent letters to rulers. Which two empires were among those addressed?
o: The Chinese and the Japanese empires of the East
The Byzantine and the Persian empires
questions.e: The letters invited rulers including Heraclius of the Byzantines and Khosrau of Persia. The other pairs were not among the rulers addressed.

questions.s: When the angel of the mountains offered to crush the people of Makkah between two mountains after the Ta'if incident, the Prophet (PBUH)
o: declined, hoping that their descendants would worship Allah alone
accepted at once without any hesitation
left the decision to Abu Bakr (RA)
questions.e: He refused and said he hoped Allah would bring from them people who would worship Him alone. This shows his mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).

questions.s: Who was the first caliph of the Muslim community after the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: Abu Bakr (RA) became the first caliph in 11 AH. Umar (RA) succeeded him, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was a famous commander but never a caliph.

questions.s: The term 'Khulafa ar-Rashidun' means
questions.e: Khulafa is the plural of khalifah, a successor, and rashidun means rightly guided. It refers to the first four caliphs after the Prophet (PBUH).

questions.s: For about how long did Abu Bakr (RA) serve as caliph?
questions.e: Abu Bakr (RA) was caliph from 632 to 634 CE, a little over two years. Ten years is closer to the caliphate of Umar (RA).

questions.s: For about how many years did Umar (RA) serve as caliph?
questions.e: Umar (RA) was caliph from 634 to 644 CE, about ten years. Two years belongs to Abu Bakr (RA).

questions.s: The caliphate of Uthman (RA) lasted about
questions.e: Uthman (RA) was caliph from 644 to 656 CE, about twelve years, the longest of the four. Ten years was the term of Umar (RA).

questions.s: The 'wars of Ridda' during the caliphate of Abu Bakr (RA) were fought against
o: rebel tribes and false claimants to prophethood
the Byzantine army that was massed in Syria
the Persian forces that held the land of Iraq
the Quraysh of Makkah who still opposed Islam
questions.e: Ridda means apostasy or rebellion. Abu Bakr (RA) dealt with it to protect the unity of the community. The Byzantine and Persian campaigns came afterwards.

questions.s: Which false claimant to prophethood was defeated at the Battle of Yamamah?
questions.e: Musaylimah, known as al-Kadhdhab, was defeated at Yamamah in 12 AH. Tulayha and al-Aswad were other false claimants who were put down elsewhere.

questions.s: Where was Abu Bakr (RA) buried?
o: In the cemetery of Jannat al-Mualla at Makkah
In the city of Jerusalem near al-Aqsa
In the city of Kufa in Iraq
Beside the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in Madinah
questions.e: Abu Bakr (RA) was buried next to the Prophet (PBUH) in the chamber of Aishah (RA) in Madinah. Umar (RA) was buried there after him.

questions.s: During whose caliphate was the Hijri calendar adopted?
questions.e: The Hijri calendar, counted from the migration to Madinah, was adopted during the caliphate of Umar (RA).

questions.s: Umar (RA) was fatally attacked while he was
o: leading the dawn prayer in the mosque
travelling to Jerusalem for a visit
distributing grain to the poor of Madinah
meeting a delegation sent from Persia
questions.e: He was stabbed by a Persian slave named Abu Lulu while leading the Fajr prayer in Madinah in 23 AH. He died a few days later.

questions.s: Jerusalem passed into Muslim hands peacefully during the caliphate of
questions.e: The Christian patriarch Sophronius agreed to surrender the city to Umar (RA) in about 638 CE. Abu Bakr (RA) died before this campaign was complete.

questions.s: The covenant that Umar (RA) gave to the people of Jerusalem guaranteed
o: the safety of their lives, property and churches
the removal of every Christian from the city
the payment of a heavy tribute in gold each year
the demolition of all the churches in the city
questions.e: The treaty promised security for the people, their property and their places of worship. It is remembered as an example of tolerance towards other faiths.

questions.s: The Battle of Qadisiyyah led to the collapse of which empire?
o: The Mongol Empire of Central Asia
questions.e: Qadisiyyah, fought in Iraq under Saad ibn Abi Waqqas (RA), broke the power of the Sasanian Persians. The Byzantines were defeated at Yarmuk.

questions.s: The Battle of Nahawand in 642 CE, known as the 'Victory of Victories', was fought in
questions.e: Nahawand ended Sasanian resistance and opened the Iranian plateau to Muslim rule. Spain was reached only in 711 CE.

questions.s: Which companion led the Muslim forces that took Egypt?
questions.e: Amr ibn al-As (RA) led the conquest of Egypt in about 639 to 642 CE. Saad (RA) commanded at Qadisiyyah.

questions.s: The first major Muslim naval battle, fought against the Byzantines in 655 CE under Uthman (RA), is known as the Battle of the
questions.e: The Battle of the Masts, also called Dhat al-Sawari, off the Anatolian coast. The Trench was fought in Madinah in 5 AH.

questions.s: Which caliph is known by the title 'Dhun-Nurayn' (Possessor of Two Lights)?
questions.e: Uthman (RA) is known by this title. Abu Bakr (RA) is known as as-Siddiq and Umar (RA) as al-Faruq.

questions.s: The caliph Ali (RA) was both the cousin and which relation of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.e: Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib and married Fatimah (RA), the Prophet's daughter. He was not a grandson.

questions.s: Which city did Ali (RA) make the capital of the caliphate?
questions.e: Ali (RA) moved the seat of government from Madinah to Kufa in Iraq. Damascus became the Umayyad capital and Baghdad the Abbasid capital.

questions.s: The public treasury of the early Muslim state was known as
questions.e: Bayt al-Mal collected zakat and other revenues and spent them for the community. Bayt al-Hikmah was a centre of learning.

questions.s: Which city was the capital of the Umayyad caliphate?
