questions.e: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus. Baghdad was founded later by the Abbasids.

questions.s: Which city was founded in 762 CE by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur as his capital?
questions.e: Baghdad, the 'City of Peace', became a centre of learning and trade. Samarra was founded later, in 836 CE.

questions.s: The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem was completed in about 691 CE under the Umayyad caliph
questions.e: Abd al-Malik built it on the Temple Mount near Masjid al-Aqsa. Walid I is associated with the Great Mosque of Damascus.

questions.s: Which commander crossed from North Africa into Spain in 711 CE, giving his name to Gibraltar?
questions.e: Jabal Tariq, meaning Mount of Tariq, became Gibraltar. Musa ibn Nusayr was his governor.

questions.s: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in the early eighth century, defeating which ruler?
questions.e: Raja Dahir of Sindh was defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim. Mahmud of Ghazni came nearly three centuries later.

questions.s: Al-Khwarizmi is best known for his work in
questions.e: His book 'al-Jabr' gave algebra its name, and the word 'algorithm' comes from his name. Medicine was the field of Ibn Sina.

questions.s: Ibn Sina's 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' (Canon of Medicine) was a famous textbook of
questions.e: The Canon was used in Europe and Asia for centuries. Ibn Sina was also a philosopher.

questions.s: Ibn al-Haytham made major contributions to the study of
questions.e: His 'Book of Optics' explained vision and light through experiments. Chemistry is associated with Jabir ibn Hayyan.

questions.s: Al-Razi (Rhazes) is credited with distinguishing between
questions.e: His treatise on smallpox and measles was among the first clear clinical descriptions. The other pairs were not his key distinction.

questions.s: Al-Zahrawi, born near Cordoba, was a famous Muslim
questions.e: His encyclopaedia Al-Tasrif described surgical instruments and methods. It was widely used in Europe.

questions.s: Ibn Rushd (Averroes) of Cordoba was famed for his commentaries on the works of
questions.e: He wrote extensive commentaries on Aristotle that influenced medieval Europe. The other three belong to Chinese, Persian and Indian traditions.

questions.s: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' is regarded as a pioneering work of
o: optics and the study of vision
history and the study of societies
questions.e: The Muqaddimah is an introduction to his history in which he studied the rise and decline of societies.

questions.s: Al-Idrisi prepared a famous world map and geographical work for the Norman king
questions.e: Al-Idrisi's 'Tabula Rogeriana' was completed for Roger II in 1154 CE.

questions.s: The famous university of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez was founded in 859 CE by
questions.e: Fatimah al-Fihri used her inheritance to found the mosque and school. The caliphs named built in other cities.

questions.s: The 'House of Wisdom' in Baghdad was a centre for
o: the trade in spices and cloth
questions.e: Under the Abbasids, scholars gathered there to translate Greek, Persian and Indian works and add their own research.

questions.s: Ibn al-Nafis, a physician of Cairo, is known for describing
o: the structure of the human eye
the cause of the plague in cities
the use of anaesthesia in surgery
questions.e: In the thirteenth century he described blood passing through the lungs. The eye was studied by Ibn al-Haytham.

questions.s: The Mamluks halted the Mongol advance at which 1260 CE battle?
questions.e: Ain Jalut, in Palestine, was fought in 1260 CE. Hattin was fought in 1187 CE and Manzikert in 1071 CE.

questions.s: The Ottoman sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in
questions.e: The city fell in 1453 CE and became Istanbul. 1526 CE was the first Battle of Panipat.

questions.s: Al-Jazari, a medieval engineer, wrote about
o: the laws of inheritance and trade
questions.e: His 'Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices' described machines such as water-raising devices and clocks.

questions.s: Which governor, later the founder of Umayyad rule, built the Muslim fleet in Syria?
questions.e: Muawiyah (RA) was governor of Syria and developed the navy in the time of Uthman (RA). Khalid (RA) and Abu Ubaidah (RA) were commanders in Syria but did not found the navy.

questions.s: Who was the second caliph of the Muslim community?
questions.e: Umar (RA) succeeded Abu Bakr (RA) in 13 AH. The others were famous commanders and companions but never became caliph.

questions.s: Ali (RA) held the office of caliph for about
questions.e: Ali (RA) became caliph in 656 CE and served until 661 CE, about four and a half to five years. Twelve years is the term of Uthman (RA).

questions.s: Which caliph set up the 'Diwan', a register of soldiers and their salaries?
questions.e: Umar (RA) created the Diwan to organise stipends for the army and the community. It was one of his administrative reforms.

questions.s: The Battle of Yarmuk in 636 CE was fought by the Muslims against the
questions.e: Yarmuk in Syria was a decisive victory over the Byzantines. The Sasanians were met at Qadisiyyah.

questions.s: Uthman (RA) is remembered for generously funding which expedition?
o: The army that fought at the Battle of Badr
The caravan of the Night Journey
The army of hardship (Jaysh al-Usra) for Tabuk
questions.e: Uthman (RA) gave large amounts of wealth and animals for the Tabuk campaign. He was not a leader at Badr.

questions.s: The principle of mutual consultation in Muslim government is called
questions.e: Shura is consultation, which the Quran praises as a trait of believers. Waqf is an endowment.

questions.s: The Abbasids replaced the Umayyads as rulers of the caliphate in about
questions.e: The Abbasid revolution succeeded in 750 CE. 661 CE marks the beginning of Umayyad rule and 1258 CE the fall of Baghdad to the Mongols.

questions.s: Cordoba was the capital of Muslim rule in
questions.e: Cordoba was the capital of Umayyad al-Andalus and a famed centre of learning. Egypt's capital was Cairo.

questions.s: Al-Biruni wrote a famous account of the land and learning of
questions.e: Kitab al-Hind describes the people and sciences of India, which he visited in the time of Mahmud of Ghazni. Spain and Egypt were not his subject.

questions.s: Ibn Battuta, a famous medieval traveller, was born in
questions.e: He was born in Tangier, in present-day Morocco, in the fourteenth century. His journeys are recorded in the Rihla.

questions.s: Salahuddin Ayyubi recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in
questions.e: He won at Hattin in 1187 CE and then took the city. 638 CE was the first Muslim conquest, 1099 CE the Crusader capture.

questions.s: Through scholars such as al-Khwarizmi, Europe learned the decimal number system with zero, which originated in
questions.e: Muslim scholars adopted the Indian numerals and passed them to Europe. The Greeks and Egyptians did not have a place-value system with zero.
